findings.summary: Item covers and spot-plate pictograms are generic and repetitive. Neighbouring covers are the same drawing with the hues swapped, some primitive stacks don't read as their subject, and plates hold two or three plain dots at about 40% of the plate. The reference's pictograms each show a distinct, readable subject built from 2–3 crescent-shaded primitives that fill 60–70% of the plate, with a sparkle tucked in.
findings.promptFix: Before drawing a cover, plate or empty-state piece, name its subject in one noun. Build that noun's own outline from 2–3 primitives, so a stranger could guess the subject without the title. Dots and a plain disc are accents and never the whole pictogram. The pictogram fills 60–70% of its plate or cover. Compare neighbouring covers: if two share the same main shape and layout, change the silhouette, the pose or the supporting shape, not only the hues. An empty state gets a full composition or a large glyph, never a lone dot pair.

findings.summary: Header-band art is the same three stickers (a disc, a cloud and a sparkle) spread far apart in the same places on every band and in every app. Several discs are split into two flat hues like a pie chart, and some are cut off by the band's edge. The reference composes each hero as one tight cluster: shapes overlap, sparkles are tucked against the edge, and shading is a same-hue crescent.
findings.promptFix: Header-band shapes form one cluster in the trailing third, never scattered stickers. Start with one large crescent-shaded disc (one hue with a darker crescent of the same hue, never two flat halves). Overlap a medium second shape (a cloud, a blob or a pill) 10–20% onto its edge in a second hue. Tuck a sparkle or a dot within 8–16px of the cluster. Keep every piece fully inside the band. Vary which shapes lead and how they overlap from area to area, so no two bands share the same layout.

findings.summary: The dashboard's live activity list is built as a build-on-view vignette, so cards that haven't triggered stay invisible. The tall saturated panel then shows one card and a faint ghost, or a large empty blue block on phones.
findings.promptFix: A vignette is an illustrative fragment, never the product's real data. Remove 'a dashboard activity card' from the vignette's places. A live feed, list or table of real records renders at once and in full, with no build animation. A panel holding a short list sizes to its content instead of stretching to match the neighbouring column. On a dashboard the stat-tile row is the one saturated field: other panels are cream (indigo at night).
findings.specRule: Where. Hero and feature sections of front pages, onboarding and feature tours; an empty state as a 40%-opacity preview of the filled screen; a bubble holding the pop-dots glyph while an answer loads; a dashboard activity card.

findings.summary: On phones the product-detail cover is treated as decorative art and moved below the details to the end of the page, so the item is never pictured near the top. The reference keeps its hero imagery up front on mobile.
findings.promptFix: In Layout adaptation, say that an image or cover representing the item itself (a product, a listing, a profile, a document) is content, not art. On narrow screens it stays directly after the title, scaled down if needed. Only decorative shapes, confetti and compositions move last.
findings.specRule: Priority on narrow screens: title and primary action first, data next, art last

findings.summary: Focus treatments are inconsistent and sometimes cruder than the reference. Top-bar nav links in two apps get a flush square outline with no offset, a focused search field keeps its resting border, and a tab-strip ring is clipped at the strip's edge. The reference's ring follows the control's shape 2px out.
findings.promptFix: Every focusable element, text links included, gets a 2px focus-ring outline at 2px offset that follows its shape: rounded for links and nav items, pill or circle for controls. Scroll containers reserve padding so the ring is never clipped.

findings.summary: A field in error loses its red border while focused and shows only the focus color, so the field the message refers to looks valid.
findings.promptFix: An input in error keeps its 2px danger border when focused. Show focus on it with a 2px focus-ring outline at 2px offset outside the danger border, so both the error and the focus stay visible.
findings.specRule: Inputs, selects | border → `color.text.secondary` | border → 2px `color.focus.ring` (the focus indicator; no outline, no glow) | — | error: 2px `color.status.danger` border

findings.summary: Phone first screens are crowded or squeezed. The dashboard shell stacks two rows of chunky nav, search and avatar pills before any content, and a glyph pushes the title into a narrow column. Header bands keep a reserved art column, so leads wrap to three or four ragged lines. On a detail page a saturated cover stacks right under a saturated band. The reference's phone keeps one compact header row, centered full-width text and one field per screen.

Some surfaces fall back to generic treatments where the reference uses warm tone. The profile form sits ungrouped on white with no cream panel or plate, unselected plan cards are outlined boxes, and on product pages the cover repeats the band's hue, so two large same-hue fields stack.

The save confirmation in settings is a small inline sparkle with green text beside the buttons, often below the first screen, where the system's ink pill toast would state it confidently. The loading state shows no text.
Glyphs on product option rows are arbitrary marks that don't relate to the options they label. The reference picks each row's glyph for its label.

notes: Review: 141/141 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/morning-shapes/0.1.0-rc.1/review-1).

The structure of the reference's language is there in all four apps: yolk and area-hue bands with sag arcs, ink and blue pills on ledges with dots, cream panels, saturated stat tiles and a convincing navy/indigo night palette. Someone who knows the reference would recognise the family at once.

What holds it below the reference is the drawing. The bands carry a stamped trio of disc, cloud and sparkle instead of a composed cluster, covers and plates repeat one disc-and-dots formula with hue swaps, and some discs are split like pie charts. The reference's warmth and character live in exactly that shape work.

Secondary gaps: crude or missing focus rings, phone first screens crowded by chrome or a reserved art column, and two spec-caused defects: a live activity feed treated as a build-on-view vignette, and errored fields losing their danger border on focus.
